---
title: EPUB format
---

Quarto can render a document to an EPUB e-book (`.epub`) by passing the
rendered document through Pandoc's own EPUB writer. Add `epub` to a
document's `format:`, or render directly from the command line:

```bash
quarto render book.qmd --to epub
```

Or in front matter / `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
format:
  epub:
    toc: true
```

The output is a standard EPUB 3 file — chapters are plain XHTML, math
renders as MathML, and the file opens in any e-reader or e-reader
preview app.

## Splitting into chapters

Pandoc splits the document into separate chapter files at each
top-level (level-1) heading by default. Use `epub-chapter-level` to
split at a deeper heading level instead — for example, to also break
out level-2 sections into their own chapter files:

```yaml
format:
  epub:
    epub-chapter-level: 2
```

## Cover image and metadata

```yaml
format:
  epub:
    epub-cover-image: cover.png
    epub-metadata: metadata.xml
```

- `epub-cover-image` sets the book's cover image (a path relative to
  the document, or to the project root when it starts with `/`).
- `epub-metadata` points at an XML file of additional
  [EPUB metadata](https://pandoc.org/MANUAL.html#epub-metadata)
  (identifier, additional contributors, series information, and so
  on) to merge into the generated `content.opf`.

## Fonts and styling

```yaml
format:
  epub:
    epub-embed-font: fonts/MyFont.ttf
    css: style.css
```

- `epub-embed-font` embeds a font file directly in the EPUB container
  so it's available even on readers that don't have it installed. It
  can be repeated to embed more than one font.
- `css` links an additional stylesheet into every chapter, on top of
  Quarto's own callout and layout styles, which are always included.

## Known limitation: tabsets

Tabbed content (`::: {.panel-tabset}`) renders in EPUB using the same
interactive tab markup as HTML output. Most EPUB readers don't run the
JavaScript that hides the inactive tabs, so **all tab panels appear
expanded, one after another**, rather than as a single active tab.
The content itself is unaffected — nothing is dropped — but the
tabbed presentation doesn't collapse the way it does in a browser.
